node-1.label: A 32-year-old woman had painless unilateral blurring of vision in her left eye for the past three months

node-2.label: Best-corrected visual acuity was 20/20 in the right eye and 20/250 in the left eye; color vision and Humphrey visual field analysis 24-2 were normal in the right eye, while the left eye exhibited severely depressed fields with central 10 degrees around fixation preserved

node-3.label: Right eye examination was normal with a cup disc ratio of 0.5; left eye showed engorged episcleral vessels, a relative afferent pupillary defect, grade III nuclear sclerosis with cortical cataract, and a cup disc ratio of 0.9 on fundus examination

node-4.label: Intraocular pressure was 16 mmHg in the right eye and 42 mmHg in the left eye by Goldman applanation tonometry; gonioscopy indicated open angles in both eyes

node-5.label: There was no proptosis or audible bruit, and extraocular movements were full

attrs.why: New Radiologist analysis supports left open-angle glaucoma as the most credible diagnosis, and the newly noted negative neuroimaging excludes secondary mass/vascular malformation. Combined with existing evidence of asymmetric visual field loss, RAPD, CDR 0.9, IOP 42 mmHg with open angles, and no orbital signs, confidence increases from 0.9 to 0.95; pending retinal nerve fiber layer OCT, dynamic IOP, and corneal thickness prevent certainty.

The Radiologist analysis states cataract is insufficient to explain the full picture and excludes it as the main cause. High IOP, RAPD, severe field loss, and CDR 0.9 all point to glaucoma, so cataract is likely a coexisting finding rather than the primary explanation; confidence decreases from 0.3 to 0.2.

Engorged episcleral vessels and open-angle high IOP keep secondary open-angle glaucoma possible, but the Radiologist notes no proptosis or bruit and negative neuroimaging, which exclude cavernous-carotid fistula, mass, and vascular malformation. These findings reduce the likelihood of a secondary mechanism relative to primary open-angle glaucoma; confidence decreases from 0.4 to 0.3.
